why: Bundles can be bought any number of times under a budget: unbounded knapsack where cost is the weight and books are the value. 'Without spending more than n' is the at-most version, so best[b] starts at 0 for every budget.
hints: Greedy by books-per-dollar fails (example 1: two 20-book bundles beat the cheaper ratio). Think of the budget as a knapsack capacity.
best[b] = most books with spending at most b. Buying one more bundle i on top of best[b - cost_i] gives best[b - cost_i] + quantity_i.
best = [0] * (n + 1); for each bundle, for b from cost up to n (upward, so it can be bought again): best[b] = max(best[b], best[b - cost] + qty). Answer best[n].
pitfalls: Starting with -infinity except best[0] would demand spending exactly b; here leftover money is fine.
A bundle costlier than the budget is never bought; the answer may be 0.
The sweep must go upward to allow repeats.
